_: THE SWEEP THAT SAYS THE WRAPPER'S SIDE OF THE FRESHNESS PASS IS NOT VACUOUS
— run it from the repository root:
cargo run -q --manifest-path tools/injection-harness/Cargo.toml -- \
crates/mnemosyne-cli/sweeps/fresh-run-cleaning.sweep.json
WHAT THE CONTRACT IS. `--fresh` is what `scripts/verify.sh` does when nobody
says otherwise: before running the command it was given, it asks
`tools/stale-artifacts` to remove the build artifacts of every package this
tree has changed, in the workspace THAT COMMAND builds. That is the second
half of the R743 repair — the lock stops two cargos racing, this recovers from
a race that already happened.
THE DECISION LIVES IN THE PROGRAM AND ITS OWN SWEEP IS BESIDE IT
(`tools/stale-artifacts/injection-sweep.json`). What is left here is the
WRAPPER'S four obligations, which is what this file is about: ask the pass,
hand it the command, run it BEFORE the verification, and fail the whole run
when it refuses. R1240 wrote this sweep against the eight lines of shell the
pass used to be; R1257 re-aimed it, because those lines are gone.
AND THE FIFTH IS IN ANOTHER FILE'S LAW: `check-side-workspaces.sh` must not
opt its twenty-three suites out again, which is the state R1257 found.
RUN IT LOCALLY. The harness edits this tree and writes the firing record
beside this file, so a run sent to a build machine leaves its evidence on a
throwaway copy (R1205's carry, and the `writes` line in the declaration).

injections.name: the-pass-is-announced-and-never-asked
injections.why: the announcement and the act are two lines, and only one of them is what a reader sees. A wrapper that prints its own freshness heading and asks nothing is indistinguishable from a working one, and what it leaves behind is exactly the stale artifact this script was written after: a deterministic regression that reads as a flake. THE SECOND RED IS THE HARNESS CORRECTING THIS MANIFEST: a wrapper that never asks the pass never hears it refuse, so removing the call takes BOTH guarantees at once. The prediction written here first named only one, and `red_set: exhaustive` is what turned that into a failure rather than a smaller number nobody read

injections.name: the-pass-is-asked-without-the-command-it-precedes
injections.why: WHICH workspace a run has to freshen is a property of the command about to run, and this repository has twenty-four of them. A pass asked without it answers about the root workspace for every one of the twenty-three separate suites — the exact state N139 named, reconstructed one word at a time

injections.name: the-pass-refusal-is-reported-and-not-honoured
injections.why: the two gates this script runs AFTER a command judge that command, so their refusals leave a run that still happened. This one runs BEFORE and guarantees a property OF the run, so a wrapper that prints the refusal and verifies anyway has a green line where the R743 warning should be — and the diff is one condition

injections.name: no-fresh-runs-the-pass-anyway
injections.why: the flag is what the workflows use, because a hosted runner's tree is a fresh clone where nothing differs from HEAD and the pass could only cost a build. A wrapper that ran it regardless makes the flag a comment, and the direction is quiet: everything still passes, every CI job just got longer

injections.name: the-separate-workspaces-opt-out-of-freshening-again
injections.why: the state this round found, and it had a comment defending it: the pass could only clean crates under `crates/`, so asking for it here freshened nothing. That reading was right and the conclusion was the wrong half of it. With the pass repaired, the flag going back is twenty-three suites silently losing R743's recovery half — and nothing else in this repository would notice
